title: Schizophrenia Explained: Biological Causes
welcome_lead: Genes, dopamine and brain structure — biology behind the symptoms.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology schizophrenia biological: genes dopamine hypothesis brain structure.
final_note: Heritability is high but environment still matters.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gottesman (1991): MZ concordance 48%, DZ 17%, lifetime risk 1% general population. Ripke et al. (2014) GWAS: 108 schizophrenia-associated SNPs — confirming a polygenic disorder. Tienari (2004) Finnish adoptees: only those raised in dysfunctional families became psychotic — diathesis-stress.

L-dopa (raises dopamine for Parkinson's) can cause psychosis. Antipsychotics block D2 receptors. Modern view: hyperdopaminergia in the mesolimbic pathway → positive symptoms; hypodopaminergia in the mesocortical pathway → negative symptoms. Glutamate may also play a role.

Chronic schizophrenia patients show enlarged ventricles (Brown et al. 1986 — 15% larger), reduced grey matter in prefrontal cortex and temporal lobe, and abnormal hippocampus. Causation is unclear — could be cause or effect of long-term medication.
